scene: SKIP: to experience something worth drawing needs a named event, such as a fall or a storm, and the drawing would read as that event; the inner half has no single picturable mark at A2.

two children stand an arm's length apart in a bare schoolyard, each facing the other with both fists raised and elbows tucked in, one boy already throwing a fist forward so the other leans back out of reach; feet apart and knees bent, mouths open and furious.
must: a fist thrown by one child while the other pulls back.
avoid: one fist held up alone with a flexed arm (kunnen); a girl lying on the ground and covering her face (vallen); two hands both closed on one long rope (trekken); two children holding hands and smiling (helpen); sticks, knives or any weapon (dreigen).
alt: Twee kinderen staan tegenover elkaar; een van hen haalt uit met de vuist, het ander leunt achteruit.
example_nl: De jongens vechten op het schoolplein.
example_en: The boys are fighting in the playground.

scene: one adult stands on a low stool in a bare room and hooks a coat by its loop onto a nail high on a plain wall with one hand; the coat already takes its weight on the nail and the hand is just letting go, both feet on the stool.
must: a coat taking its weight on a nail as the hand lets go.
avoid: one adult flat on their back on a bed (liggen); a person upright beside a bicycle (staan); clothes folded in a neat pile (leggen); a framed picture on the wall (bekijken); a hook with nothing on it.
alt: Een volwassene op een krukje schuift met een hand een jas over een spijker hoog aan de muur.
example_nl: De jas hangt aan de haak.
example_en: The coat hangs on the hook.

scene: one adult stands at a kitchen counter, full figure head to feet, holding a long thin wooden skewer horizontally in both hands; four large vegetable chunks are already threaded on it and the sharp point sticks out past the last chunk. No knife, no chopping board.
must: a long skewer with vegetable chunks threaded on it and the point sticking out.
avoid: a knife cutting through a carrot (snijden); a needle taken through cloth (naaien); a fork lifted to the mouth (eten); a key turning in a door (wonen); a spade in the ground (graven).
alt: Iemand staat aan het aanrecht en houdt met beide handen een lange houten prikker vast met grote stukken groente erop; de scherpe punt komt aan het eind uit.
example_nl: Ik steek de stekker in het stopcontact.
example_en: I put the plug into the socket.

scene: one adult stands beside a fresh mound of turned earth in a small garden, full figure head to feet with the feet visible, a spade in one hand with its blade on the ground, and with the other hand lays a few cut flowers flat on top of the mound. No marker, no hole, no body.
must: a fresh mound of earth with cut flowers being laid on it.
avoid: a small tree pressed into a garden hole (planten); a spade lifting soil out of a trench (graven); a gravestone or any marker; three people with heads bowed; a person kneeling to look under a sofa (zoeken).
alt: Iemand staat met een schop bij een verse hoop aarde en legt er een paar bloemen op.
example_nl: De hond wil zijn bot begraven.
example_en: The dog wants to bury its bone.

scene: SKIP: proving is an argument landing, and a person adding up on an abacus would show the sum and not the proof; proving has no single action of its own.

one adult stands at a kitchen counter with a small kitchen scale in front of them, a paper bag of apples resting in its flat pan, the needle of the dial swung round to the right; one hand still steadies the bag and the eyes are on the dial.
must: a filled bag pulling the needle of a kitchen scale round.
avoid: a hand under the chin and eyes rolled up (denken); two pans on a balance (rechtspreken); a market trader with a note (kopen); a tape measure or a ruler (meten).
alt: Een volwassene zet een volle zak appels op een keukentoestel met een wijzer en kijkt naar die wijzer.
example_nl: Hoeveel weegt jouw koffer?
example_en: How much does your suitcase weigh?

scene: one adult stands in the middle of an empty street with both hands cupped round the mouth, mouth wide open and eyes on a distant figure at the far end of the street, who is already turning round; between them the street is bare, no letter or word in the air.
must: two cupped hands round an open mouth calling to a far figure.
avoid: two people close together with speech bubbles (praten); a telephone held to one ear (bellen); one hand flat beside the mouth with a whisper (fluisteren); a raised arm shaking a fist (vechten); a horn or a bell (luiden).
alt: Een volwassene heeft beide handen aan de open mond, gericht naar iemand die ver weg op straat omkijkt.
example_nl: Mijn moeder roept ons voor het eten.
example_en: My mother calls us for dinner.

scene: one very old adult lies on a bed seen from the side, full figure, with both eyes closed and both hands folded on the blanket, face calm and still, mouth one short horizontal line with no upturned corners (not a smile); a plain wooden chair stands empty beside the bed on the viewer's side, between the bed and the side table, and on the side table a short candle stub with melted wax pooled at its base burns with one tiny flame.
must: an old person lying still with folded hands and a burned-down candle.
avoid: both hands pressed on one chest (zijn); hands held up towards the sky beside a bed (bidden); a person asleep with a snore mark (slapen); a doctor beside a bed with a clipboard (onderzoeken); a cross or a headstone (begraven).
alt: Een heel oude mens ligt met gevouwen handen op bed; naast het bed brandt een kaarsje bijna op.
example_nl: Veel oude bomen sterven door de droogte.
example_en: Many old trees die because of the drought.

scene: SKIP: discussing is talking over a subject; the best picture is two people with a bar each above the head, which is praten on the A1 page, and adding papers would only turn it into spreken.

one adult stands still on a bare floor, seen from the side, full figure head to feet with white margin. The head, chest and arms are drawn solid cobalt; from the waist down the body turns into a thin dashed contour line (plain dashes, no dots, no dot-fill, no gradient) that thins out to nothing at the feet, so the legs and feet are nearly gone. Only the figure; no door, no field, no other object, no symbol.
must: a standing person whose lower body fades away into a dashed outline.
avoid: a person stepping through a doorway (verlaten); an empty pair of shoes left behind (vergeten); a dove or a ball leaving a hat (toverslaan); a person with an eye to a microscope (onderzoeken); smoke from a fire (branden).
alt: Iemand staat stil; vanaf het middel naar beneden lost het lichaam op in een stippellijn die bij de voeten bijna weg is.
example_nl: Mijn bril is ineens verdwenen.
example_en: My glasses have suddenly disappeared.

scene: one adult is seen from the side swimming in a pool: a bold pool edge and a wavy water-surface line are drawn, the body lies nearly horizontal just under the surface line with the head and one arm stretched forward out of the water, the other arm sweeping back, both legs kicking behind under the surface, goggles on and eyes ahead. Not a dive and not a leap.
must: an arm stretched forward over the water with the head up.
avoid: a body already entering the water head first with both arms ahead (duiken); feet at the shallow end and a hand on the ladder (stappen); a board under both hands (drijven); a towel and a deckchair on the tiles (liggen); a boat or a sail (varen).
alt: Iemand in het bad steekt een arm vooruit boven het water, terwijl de benen achter hem trappelen.
example_nl: In de zomer zwemmen wij in het meer.
example_en: In summer we swim in the lake.

scene: SKIP: keeping is houden, the same box held to the chest (review M8).

one adult stands in a bare room with both arms swept out wide to the sides and one leg lifted half off the floor, caught mid-swing; short repeated curved strokes trail in the air behind the arms and behind the lifted foot and nowhere else in the frame.
must: an arm swung wide beside a foot leaving the floor.
avoid: the front foot flat and the back foot just lifted, arms swinging in opposition (lopen); a person standing straight with arms along the body (staan); a body flat on a bed with eyes open (liggen); a still statue on a plinth (staan); a marching band (marcheren).
alt: Iemand staat met de armen wijd in een lege kamer, een been van de vloer, korte strepen achter de armen.
example_nl: Ik moet meer bewegen.
example_en: I need to move more.

scene: one adult with a suitcase in one hand stands at the right edge of the frame, seen from behind, with the front foot already over the threshold of an open doorway, head turned away towards the empty road outside. A second adult stands still inside the room at the left, empty-handed, facing the back of the first.
must: one adult with a suitcase already stepping out through a doorway.
avoid: one adult alone with arms swinging towards a shut door (gaan); a bicycle rolled out of a shed onto a street (fietsen); a fist raised against a second person (aanvallen); a hand raised flat on a door to shut it (sluiten); a train on a platform.
alt: Iemand met een koffer stapt door de open deur naar buiten; binnen blijft een ander staan.
example_nl: De trein vertrekt over vijf minuten.
example_en: The train departs in five minutes.

scene: SKIP: existing has no action and nothing to point at; the only honest picture would be a person standing alone, which is the picture of zijn on the A0 page, and no other symbol is allowed here.

one adult stands beside a second adult and stretches one arm out straight towards a fire extinguisher fixed to the far wall, the index finger level with it, head turned the same way; the second adult, a step behind and to the side, follows the line of the pointing arm with their eyes.
must: an outstretched arm with one finger aimed at a wall object.
avoid: an open flat palm held towards a person by a door (mogen); a hand held flat beside the temple to shade the eyes (kijken); a finger raised straight up beside an open mouth (roepen); a hand round a pencil on paper (schrijven); an arrow on a sign (leiden).
alt: Een volwassene strekt de arm met een gestrekte vinger naar een brandblusser aan de muur, terwijl een tweede persoon meekijkt.
example_nl: Hij wijst naar de kerk.
example_en: He points at the church.

scene: SKIP: suffering has no visible action of its own; a frowning face or a bandage on an arm is the picture of pijn or gewond rather than a verb.
SKIP: a formal modal; the only picture would be the flexed arm of kunnen.
SKIP: dying is drawn on the sterven card; a second deathbed would be the same picture.
SKIP: undertaking is abstract; any single action would be another verb.

one adult stands facing the viewer on a beach, full figure head to feet with a short ground line under the feet, both palms facing up with the fingers curled and the hands touching side by side a metre in front of the chest, a small round ball sitting inside the cupped hands and touching both palms (not above them), eyes on the ball; both feet stay planted flat on the sand.
must: a ball caught between two cupped hands on flat feet.
avoid: one hand closing on a mug and lifting it off a shelf (pakken); a hand gripping another person by the wrist (redden); an outstretched arm with an open empty palm (vragen); a ball bouncing off the fingertips (spelen); a dog running after a stick (gooien).
alt: Iemand staat op het strand met de handen hol voor de borst, en de bal landt net tussen de handpalmen.
example_nl: De keeper kan de bal vangen.
example_en: The goalkeeper can catch the ball.

scene: SKIP: thinking up something new has no picture of its own; the bubble and the lightbulb belong to denken and weten on the A0 page and are banned at A2.

one adult stands with both hands resting on the top of a long flat wooden plank held out in front, the two halves already dropping away from each other at a jagged line at its middle, a few short splinters in the air; the eyes are down on the break. Everything is cobalt outline only: the plank is a plain blank white bar with a bold cobalt outline, with no ticks, numbers, lines or notches anywhere on it, even along its edges; the splinters are short cobalt strokes; no beige, tan or wood-coloured fill.
must: a long plank snapping in two under two hands.
avoid: a mug already in pieces on the floor (vallen); a screwdriver in a screw (gebruiken); a hammer and a nail (maken); a hand patting a torn cloth (repareren); a wall of bricks on the ground (bouwen).
alt: Iemand houdt twee handen op een lange lat die in het midden knapt, met splinters in de lucht.
example_nl: Pas op, dan breek je het glas.
example_en: Be careful, or you will break the glass.

scene: one adult is caught in mid-air over bare ground, seen from the side, full figure, torso upright and leaning slightly forward, thighs forward with the shins tucked up under the body, both arms swung back behind; a clear ground line is drawn well below the feet, the feet well clear of the ground and the figure fully detached from it, eyes on something ahead of the landing spot.
must: a whole person in the air with both feet well above the ground.
avoid: the front foot flat and the back on its toes with arms swinging (lopen); a body tipping sideways with both arms flung out (vallen); two adults hopping in a line (dansen); a swimmer over a pool (duiken); a trampoline (stuiteren); a shadow on the ground (vallen).
alt: Iemand is met opgetrokken knieen in de lucht, de voeten hoog boven de grond en de armen naar achteren.
example_nl: De kinderen springen in het water.
example_en: The children jump into the water.

scene: SKIP: modern use is idiom (in werking treden, optreden); the stair scene is stappen (review H9).

one adult stands at a table between two apples that sit an arm's length apart and slowly turns the head from the left apple to the right; a hand is held above each apple, each hand horizontal with the palm facing down like a lid and the fingers pointing forward, hovering a thumb's width over its apple, not vertical and not palm-out; the two hands are held at exactly the same height above the two apples.
must: two hands held level above two separate apples.
avoid: one hand hovering above one of two jars (kiezen); a face card held above a head (kennen); two pans on a balance (wegen); a person with an eye to a microscope (onderzoeken); a price tag on either apple (kopen).
alt: Een volwassene kijkt van de ene appel naar de andere en houdt beide handen op precies dezelfde hoogte erboven.
example_nl: Wij vergelijken de prijzen van twee winkels.
example_en: We compare the prices of two shops.

scene: SKIP: guessing is an inner act; the closest visible act is asking, which is praten on another page, and the question mark in a cloud is an A0 mark.
SKIP: defeating is the moment of winnen seen from the other side; same picture.
SKIP: the same picture as a person stepping through a doorway (gaan) or walking out of mist (verdwijnen); the difference needs two frames.
SKIP: there is no picture of its own that is not a speech bubble, which is praten on another page; a long nose or crossed fingers is a cartoon mark, not a scene.
SKIP: turning out is a judgement about what something really was, which is idiom and not a scene; nothing visible separates it from vinden or denken.
SKIP: maintaining is a routine, and any single moment reads as repareren.
one adult stands facing a second adult and holds one hand behind the back, the fingers closed round a small key that the second adult cannot see; the free hand rests at the side and the face is calm.
must: an object held out of sight behind the back.
avoid: a back pressed against a door (zich verstoppen); a hand reaching under a cushion (zoeken); a key held out to a second person (geven); both hands over the eyes (spelen).
alt: Iemand staat tegenover een ander en houdt een sleutel achter de rug.
example_nl: Het kind wil zich achter de bank verbergen.
example_en: The child wants to hide behind the sofa.

scene: SKIP: referring is abstract; the picture would be the pointing arm of wijzen.

one adult sits at a plain table facing a second adult across it, full figure, mouth shut, with the index finger lying horizontally across both closed lips, the fingertip reaching the opposite cheek, the finger crossing the mouth and not pointing up beside the face; eyes level and steady. The other adult has an open mouth and both hands lifted, and no speech bubble touches the silent one.
must: a finger laid across closed lips at a shared table.
avoid: two people close together with speech bubbles (praten); a mouth wide open and two cupped hands (roepen); a telephone held to one ear (bellen); a hand raised flat for silence (waarschuwen); a crossed-out mouth (weigeren).
alt: Iemand legt een vinger overdwars op de lippen, terwijl de persoon aan de overkant van tafel net iets wil zeggen.
example_nl: De leerlingen zwijgen als de leraar binnenkomt.
example_en: The pupils fall silent when the teacher comes in.

scene: one adult kneels beside a bed with both elbows resting on the mattress edge and both hands pressed palm to palm under the chin, eyes closed and head bowed; a short plain candle with a small flame burns on the bedside table and nothing else is in the room.
must: two palms pressed together under a bowed head.
avoid: two hands clasped beneath a small umbrella (hopen); a person on a chair with the chin on a fist (denken); a figure seated before a computer (werken); a stained cross, a mosque or a church window (geloven); a rosary with beads.
alt: Een volwassene knielt bij een bed met de handen tegen elkaar onder de kin, ogen dicht, naast een kaars.
example_nl: Zij bidden elke avond voor het eten.
example_en: They pray every evening before dinner.

scene: SKIP: designing at a drawing table is the picture of tekenen.
SKIP: expiring or going a certain way is abstract; a date passing needs digits.
SKIP: a decision has no single picturable action; a fork in the road would read as kiezen and a gavel as rechtspreken.
SKIP: remembering is inner; any scene is an invented sign (review M9).
SKIP: a rule applying is idiom; a sign with a tick or a cross needs letters and a symbol, and neither is allowed on this page.
SKIP: loading a van is the lossen picture with the direction reversed.

a small car ferry crosses a wide river, seen from the side, with a low bow wave and a curl of wake behind; one adult stands at the rail on deck looking across the water to the far bank. No sail and no flag.
must: a ferry under way on a river with a wake behind.
avoid: a sail curved by the wind (zeilen); a rower with both oars in the water (roeien); a swimmer (zwemmen); a boat tied up at a jetty (aanmeren); a person on a bridge over the river (lopen).
alt: Een veerpont steekt een brede rivier over; iemand staat aan de reling en kijkt naar de overkant.
example_nl: De veerboot vaart elk uur naar het eiland.
example_en: The ferry sails to the island every hour.

scene: SKIP: avoiding is turning away from one thing while aiming at the other, so it needs both the thing avoided and the goal; the only honest picture is a near-miss, which reads as wijken on this page.
SKIP: telling things apart is inner; the picture would be vergelijken.
SKIP: to be called is located in a name and a name is letters; writing the word in the drawing is forbidden.
SKIP: something missing IS the empty place, and an empty place cannot be seen without the thing that should be there; the picture would show the object or its absence, never the verb.

one adult is caught just above the water of a swimming pool in an arched dive, seen from the side, full figure: the head and arms point straight down with the fingertips one hand's width above the water and not yet touching it, both knees visibly bent with the shins folded up so the feet are the highest point. The water is only a plain wavy surface line; no slab, edge, board or platform anywhere.
must: fingertips a hand's width above the water, feet highest.
avoid: an arm stretched forward over the water with the head up (zwemmen); a foot on the pool ladder (stappen); a body already under the surface (zwemmen); a board under both hands (drijven); a boat with sails (varen); a springboard with a crowd (springen).
alt: Een zwemmer is in een boog boven het water: de handen gaan recht naar beneden en de voeten staan hoog.
example_nl: De zwemmer duikt in het diepe water.
example_en: The swimmer dives into the deep water.

scene: SKIP: staying somewhere is a state; the picture would be wonen or blijven.
SKIP: opposing something abstract has no visible action, and the literal sense is the fist fight already drawn for vechten on this page.
SKIP: obtaining is krijgen in a formal register; same picture.

one adult stands at a low washbasin on a pedestal, full figure from head to feet with the legs and feet visible below the basin, and rubs both palms together centred directly under the tap: the spout is directly above the rubbing hands and the whole stream falls from the spout straight onto the hands (one stream only, not beside them); soapsuds up the wrists and a few drops on the basin rim; the eyes are down on the hands and a small towel hangs on a rail beside the basin.
must: both hands rubbed together under a running tap.
avoid: a shower head over a head (douchen); a hand scrubbing a plate under a tap (afwassen); a body standing in a bath tub (baden); a washing machine with its door open (de was doen); a hand on a tap handle (draaien).
alt: Iemand wrijft de handen met zeep onder een lopende kraan, met de ogen op de handen en een handdoek ernaast.
example_nl: Ik was mijn handen voor het eten.
example_en: I wash my hands before dinner.

scene: One adult stands at a laid table and pours a drink from a bottle into a glass standing in front of a seated guest. The stream is caught mid-air, the glass a third full. The guest watches the glass. A second empty glass stands on the table.
must: a bottle pouring a stream into a guest's glass.
avoid: a note dropped into a donation chest (schenken); a glass raised for a toast (proosten); a person drinking from a glass (drinken); water poured from a bucket over plants (gieten); coffee made in a machine (zetten).
alt: Een volwassene giet vanuit een fles een straal drank in het glas van een gast die aan tafel zit.
example_nl: Mag ik je nog een glas schenken?
example_en: May I pour you another glass?
